properties.decision:
DECIDED by Anthony 2026-07-31, on three calls put to him after the mechanism was measured rather than assumed. His original framing is preserved in the snapshot at `snap:epoch:arrival-delta:dec:arrival-delta`.

WHAT ARRIVES, PER SCHEDULED ITEM — his three outcomes, the complement he did not name, and a FIFTH his four assume away:
  - DELIVERED — the plan held. Computed from the golden thread (`req:completion-computed`), never asserted.
  - DEFERRED — still intended, the date moved; the report names where it now points.
  - DISCONTINUED — no longer intended at all. Distinct from deferred the way `retire-from-design` distinguishes them: one is a date change, the other a withdrawal.
  - DELIVERED BUT NEVER PLANNED — reported as `added_after_baseline`, work scheduled here after the commitment was taken. A delta measured only against the plan cannot see the work that was not in it, and that is usually where the estimate went.
  - OUTSTANDING — still pointed at a moment that has arrived, and not delivered. THE FOUR ASSUME EVERY UNDELIVERED ITEM WAS CONSCIOUSLY MOVED OR DROPPED, and the commonest case is that nobody touched it and it did not happen. Calling that `discontinued` would put a withdrawal on the record nobody made; calling it `deferred` would invent a date nobody chose. It is exactly the question `req:plans-move-honestly` says must be ASKED and never defaulted — transferred or discontinued — so it is reported as its own outcome and put to the user.

CALL 1 — THE BASELINE IS THE TARGET'S FIRST SNAPSHOT, with every later one returned as the movement trail. The brainstorm said the LAST snapshot, and that does not compute what he asked for: two replans leave epoch 3 holding {A,B,C} then {A,C}, so reading the last says the plan was always {A,C} and B's slip vanishes from the very report meant to show it. Where no snapshot exists the plan has never been recorded as moving, so the live edges ARE the original plan and are the baseline — stated as `BaselineSource`, not implied. ACCEPTED WRINKLE, named rather than hidden: the baseline is whenever a snapshot first happened to be taken, which may predate the plan being complete; where the baseline captured an empty plan the report says so in `notes` and the trail shows the growth.

CALL 2 — `snapshot_node` EXCLUDES BY EDGE ROLE, NOT ENDPOINT TYPE. See `dec:commitment-edges-survive-snapshots`, minted for it.

CALL 3 — A LOSSY SCHEDULE EDIT WITH NO RECORDED CHANGE IS REFUSED, mirroring `record_change` refusing a planned epoch. Removing a `SCHEDULED_FOR`, re-pointing it, or rewriting its modality all destroy a claim; each is refused while the plan is unrecorded, with the refusal naming the `record_change` that unblocks it. ADDING to a plan is deliberately NOT guarded — it destroys no earlier claim, and taxing it would punish correct work, which is the mistake this project keeps finding in detectors. `delete_node` is guarded from both directions too, because retiring a scheduled requirement is precisely how discontinuation happens and would otherwise walk straight past the refusal.

WHAT IS COMPUTED VERSUS STORED, unchanged and load-bearing: NOTHING about the outcome is written down. The plan lives in the epoch's snapshots, delivery is computed from the thread, and storing the result would create a second source of truth able to disagree with the first — the same argument that keeps `achieved` out of the `modality` enum.

WHAT FALLS OUT: `missed_obligations`, the `required` claims that did not land — computed violations rather than slips, and the scheduling face of a KPP. And once several epochs have arrived, the confidence `req:plans-move-honestly` wants a planned claim to carry can be MEASURED from arrival history rather than authored — Anthony's Black-Scholes analogy, answered with observation.

DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: delivery is not dated to an epoch, so "delivered during this window but never scheduled anywhere" is not computable and is not claimed. `added_after_baseline` answers the narrower, answerable question, and `notes` says which one was answered.
properties.name: What happens when an epoch arrives: the delta is computed against the FIRST snapshot, and a lossy schedule edit is refused
properties.rationale:
MEASURED BEFORE DECIDED, and two of the three calls exist because the measuring found something the brainstorm had not.

The mechanism claim held: `snapshot_node` really does chain incoming edges, so snapshotting the epoch captures every schedule edge pointing at it — the whole plan in one call. And `record_change`'s planned-epoch refusal keys on the epoch you FILE INTO, not the node you snapshot, so a replan files into the current arrived epoch with the planned epoch as its subject. That also answers the open question inside `cap:plan-movement-recorded`: filing in the arrived epoch is sufficient, and planned epochs need no revision chain of their own.

But the trap was WORSE than the brainstorm stated, which is call 2. And "the last snapshot" would have under-reported exactly the slip the report exists to show, which is call 1. Both were found by reading the code rather than reasoning about it — the same method that found the wrong-direction edge in `dec:epoch-pins-a-version-combination`.

The fifth outcome came from asking what happens to an item nobody touches, which is the ordinary case and the one the four-outcome framing has no room for. Forcing it into `discontinued` or `deferred` would have made the report assert a decision that was never taken — the failure `dec:report-dont-judge` exists to prevent, arriving through a vocabulary that was simply too small.

Mutation-checked, all three calls: empty the commitment-edge list and the snapshot test fails; take the baseline from the last snapshot instead of the first and the two-replan test fails; make the guard always allow and all three refusal tests fail.
